# Independent first qmatch authoring

Two separately authorized model authors received the frozen English Reference,
README, STDLIB and five tasks, without this chat, live implementation, other
authors or compiler feedback. Their original disclosures identify the actual
context and sections read. This is a context-disclosed first-authoring study,
not a model success-rate benchmark.

The inert [archive](first.tar.xz) and [inventory](first-index.json.xz) retain all
ten unchanged sources and manifests, original notes, task, participant input
hashes and complete first CLI stdout/stderr. The twenty Reference files are
pinned by immutable Git commit/path/size/hash rather than duplicated. The
passive history test reads bytes only; it never executes archived commands.

Six positive open functions pass the existing selected typed-root checker.
Both ordinary matches over live quantum owners refuse. Both duplicate/missing
partitions refuse at duplicate ordinal 1; that observation does not independently
test the missing-label condition. No first source was repaired.

The positive JSON reports `source_steps_checked`, `source_meaning_verified` and
`source_preservation_verified` as false, with producer-origin runtime requests
and `checked-produced-ir` execution authority. Executable hashes identify the
existing observed binaries, not a fresh source build or binary attestation.

Separate root-authored exact-operator and corpus experiments, their original
artifacts, observer code and earlier scaffold failures remain external and are
not archive members. Their checkpoint distinguishes six exact Rust operator
tests from the unsuccessful independent native functional-request attempt.
Neither these observations nor retention completes #64/#195, source/runtime
preservation, a constitutional obligation or release readiness.
